text:
Matvei Gridin is 20 years old, two seasons removed from the 28th pick, and already playing 16:20 a night in Calgary. Six goals and 14 points in 25 games is a strong rookie-level start, and a headline this month argued Ryan Huska should keep him with Matt Coronato. Our numbers say they play a lot alike.

He drives play more than most first-year forwards: the Flames' share of expected goals is 5.4 points better with him on the ice than off. He carries the puck into the zone on 61% of his entries in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, and carry-ins lead to chances three times as often as dump-ins. The finishing is running a bit hot (six goals on 4.5 expected), so don't expect the goal pace to climb. Five of his points have come on the power play. His last junior season, 79 points in Shawinigan, translated to about 32 NHL points. Our range projects 40 to 61 points, a good season for a player still learning the league.
